newsitem.title: USA: Waigel says G7 statement meant to be stronger.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says G7 statement meant to be stronger.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said the statement from the weekend Group of Seven meeting in Washington was meant to be stronger than the statement issued at the G7 meeting in Berlin last February.
In response to a reporter's question, Waigel said, "It was planned that it (the G7 communique) was stronger than the statement made in Berlin."

But the statement gave no hint of intervention threats or approximate target levels for exchange rates. The statement said that the G7 nations had "agreed to monitor developments and to cooperate as appropriate in exchange markets".
In Tokyo trade on Monday, following the release of the communique, the dollar briefly hit a 37-month high of 1.7389 marks and rose sharply to 127.08 yen, near its 55-month high at 127.16 yen.
At 1225 EDT/1725 GMT, dollar/mark traded at 1.7237/47 compared to 1.7320/30 at Monday's close and dollar/yen changed hands at 126.75 yen from 126.83/88 .
